prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates, inside a new VPC with a 10.0.0.0/16 CIDR block, a two-tier security group configuration for routing traffic through an Application Load Balancer to backend EC2 instances. The first security group, named "alb", should accept inbound HTTP traffic on port 80 from any IP address and permit outbound traffic only within the VPC CIDR. The second security group, named "allow_alb", must be configured to accept inbound HTTP traffic on port 80 exclusively from the ALB security group, while also allowing outbound traffic only within the VPC CIDR.

We need a Terraform template that creates a basic networking stack for infrastructure deployment, with the AWS region defaulting to "us-east-1". The core network must consist of a VPC with DNS support and hostnames enabled, using a configurable CIDR block that defaults to "10.0.0.0/16" and tagged as "main-vpc". Additionally, provision subnets dynamically across specified availability zones, defaulting to the first two availability zones in the region with default subnet CIDR blocks of "10.0.1.0/24" and "10.0.2.0/24", where each subnet is individually tagged with an index-based name following the pattern "main-subnet-N".

We need a Terraform template that creates an IAM role and custom policy allowing an AWS Managed Grafana workspace named "Grafana" to query Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and CloudWatch metrics, restricting assumption of the role to specified monitoring AWS accounts.

We need a Terraform template that creates a VPC with public and private subnets across two availability zones and a single NAT gateway, a security group that allows SSH only from within the VPC CIDR, allows HTTP, HTTPS, and application ports 3000 and 5432 from anywhere, and limits outbound traffic to the VPC CIDR, plus a private Service Discovery DNS namespace named "service.local", to support containerized applications.

We need a Terraform template that creates a Cognito User Pool with an app client, an Identity Pool linked to it, and an IAM role that authenticated identities can assume for Cognito Sync and Mobile Analytics access.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile AWS KMS module capable of managing customer master keys, replica keys, imported external key material, aliases, and key grants for centralized encryption management. The template must support mutually exclusive creation flags to provision either a standard customer-managed KMS key with AWS-provided key material, an external KMS key with base64 key material, a standard multi-region replica key referencing a primary key ARN, or a replica external key with custom key material and primary external key ARN. Key policy generation must be dynamically constructed based on role inputs, supporting a default root policy, key owners, administrators, standard key users, service users, EC2 Auto Scaling roles, specific cryptographic operation users (symmetric, HMAC, asymmetric public encryption, asymmetric sign/verify), Route 53 DNSSEC signing service permissions, and custom policy statements or override documents. Finally, the module should provision KMS aliases using exact names or name prefixes, as well as KMS grants with grantee principals, allowed operations, retiring principals, and optional encryption context constraint subsets.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-cluster Kubernetes networking foundation to support cross-cluster communication testing across three availability zones. The stack must deploy a VPC using the official AWS VPC module with a CIDR block of "10.0.0.0/16", configured with a single NAT gateway to service three private subnets calculated using a prefix length extension of 4 (e.g., /20 subnets at netnums 0, 1, 2) and three public subnets calculated using a prefix length extension of 8 starting at offset 48 (e.g., /24 subnets at netnums 48, 49, 50). The public subnets must be tagged with "kubernetes.io/role/elb" set to 1, the private subnets tagged with "kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb" set to 1, and all resources tagged with Blueprint matching the VPC name and GithubRepo set to "github.com/aws-ia/terraform-aws-eks-blueprints". Additionally, provision two dedicated security groups within the VPC, named "cluster1_additional_sg" and "cluster2_additional_sg", where each security group has ingress and egress rules allowing all protocols only to and from the other cluster's security group, enabling reciprocal cross-cluster communication between cluster1 and cluster2.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, highly configurable AWS Cognito User Pool stack to manage user authentication, client app integration, and custom domain routing. The template must declare default variables for the pool name ("Pool name"), alias attributes (["email", "phone_number"]), auto-verified attributes (defaulting to empty), email verification message ("Some message {####}"), email verification subject ("Some subject"), MFA configuration ("OPTIONAL"), SMS authentication message ("SMS authentication message {####}"), SMS verification message ("SMS verification message {####}"), verification message template by link, SMS configuration map (with empty external ID and SNS caller ARN), recovery mechanisms (verified_email with priority 2, verified_phone_number with priority 1), invite message templates, admin create user only flag (defaulting to false), software token MFA enabling (defaulting to true), case sensitivity option (defaulting to null), dynamic device configuration parameters (defaulting to null), optional Lambda trigger configuration map (defaulting to empty), and custom schema definitions (defaulting to a required, mutable string email attribute). The module must conditionally provision SMS configuration when both external ID and SNS caller ARN are non-empty, software token MFA, username case sensitivity, device configuration, custom email sender Lambda triggers, and handle schema definitions with or without min/max string constraints while ignoring changes to estimated_number_of_users. Additionally, support dynamic iteration over a list of client app names defaulting to empty, creating User Pool Clients configured with generate_secret defaulting to false, token validities (access token: 120, ID token: 120, refresh token: 7) paired with token_validity_units (access_token: "minutes", id_token: "minutes", refresh_token: "days"), allowed OAuth user pool client flag (defaulting to false), token revocation (defaulting to true), explicit auth flows (["ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH", "ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH", "ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH"]), prevent_user_existence_errors ("LEGACY"), and configurable read/write attributes, callback URLs, logout URLs, OAuth flows, OAuth scopes, and supported identity providers. Furthermore, conditionally create a Cognito user group when a group name variable is non-empty (accepting precedence defaulting to 0 and an optional IAM role ARN), a Cognito User Pool domain when a domain string variable is non-empty (accepting an optional ACM certificate ARN), and an alias Route 53 A-record targeting the domain CloudFront distribution ARN (using fixed CloudFront zone ID "Z2FDTNDATAQYW2") when a create_route53_record boolean flag defaulting to false is set to true alongside a provided Route 53 zone ID.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom three-subnet VPC network layout with public and private routing capabilities to support general application deployment testing. The configuration must declare variables for a VPC CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", VPC name defaulting to "DevOps-Project-VPC", Internet Gateway name defaulting to "devops-project-igw", route table name defaulting to "DevOps-project-RT", public subnet identifier name defaulting to "subnet_a", NAT gateway name defaulting to "DevOps-NAT-GW", and a public IPv4 pool name defaulting to "amazon". It must define three subnets with configurable CIDR blocks, availability zones, public IP mapping flags, and name tags, defaulting as follows: Subnet A with CIDR "10.0.1.0/24", the first availability zone in the region, and name "Subnet-A-Public"; Subnet B with CIDR "10.0.2.0/24", the second availability zone in the region, and name "Subnet-B-Private"; and Subnet C with CIDR "10.0.3.0/24", a third, distinct availability zone in the region, and name "Subnet-C-Private", with automatic public IP assignment on launch disabled by default for all three subnets. The VPC must enable DNS support and hostnames, attach the tagged Internet Gateway, and include a route table tagged with the route table name that contains a default route to the internet via the Internet Gateway, associated explicitly only with Subnet A. Additionally, provision a VPC-scoped Elastic IP drawn from the configured public IPv4 pool to deploy a NAT gateway tagged with the NAT gateway name inside Subnet B with an explicit dependency on the Internet Gateway, alongside a custom security group tagged "DefaultSecurityGroup" within the VPC that permits outbound egress traffic only within the VPC CIDR, and output the NAT gateway's public IP.

We need a Terraform template that creates a flexible AWS Transit Gateway module to support central hub-and-spoke network routing and cross-account RAM sharing. The template must include a create boolean variable defaulting to true to toggle between provisioning a new Transit Gateway or looking up an existing one (via an id variable defaulting to null or filtering by a name tag defaulting to null). When creating the Transit Gateway, both default route table association and default route table propagation must be explicitly disabled, while allowing configuration of BGP ASN defaulting to 65200, auto_accept_shared_attachments, dns_support, vpn_ecmp_support, and transit_gateway_cidr_blocks (which validates that all entries are valid IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs). Additionally, process a map of route_tables where each item conditionally creates a new Transit Gateway route table or looks up an existing one using a transit-gateway-id filter paired with a tag:Name filter, assigning route table tags from merged global tags, local_tags, and a fallback name tag equal to the table name or the main resource name. Finally, if a shared_principals map variable contains entries, provision an AWS RAM resource share that permits external principals, defaulting its share name to an explicit ram_resource_share_name variable or the main resource name, associate the Transit Gateway to the share, and attach each principal specified in the map.

We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-subnet VPC network stack distributed across two availability zones for infrastructure testing. The template must define variables for tagging including projectPrefix (defaulting to "f5-dcec"), resourceOwner (defaulting to "f5-user"), buildSuffix (defaulting to "YY"), and map_public_ip_on_launch (defaulting to false), alongside an awsRegion variable defaulting to "us-east-1". Two optional availability zone variables (awsAz1 and awsAz2, both defaulting to null) must resolve to the first and second available availability zones in the region if unassigned, noting a logic requirement where awsAz2 falls back to referencing awsAz1 when specified. The core VPC must use a CIDR block configurable via vpcMainCidr (defaulting to "10.1.0.0/16"). Across the two resolved availability zones, create six total subnets: two public subnets using vpcMainSubPubACidr ("10.1.10.0/24") and vpcMainSubPubBCidr ("10.1.110.0/24") mapped with the map_public_ip_on_launch setting; two management subnets using vpcMainSubMgmtACidr ("10.1.1.0/24") and vpcMainSubMgmtBCidr ("10.1.101.0/24"); and two private subnets using vpcMainSubPrivACidr ("10.1.20.0/24") and vpcMainSubPrivBCidr ("10.1.120.0/24"). Additionally, create an internet gateway for the VPC, a custom route table routing all outbound traffic "0.0.0.0/0" to the internet gateway, and assign this route table explicitly as the VPC main route table association.

We need a Terraform template that creates an isolated private VPC networking infrastructure with S3 gateway endpoint access for secure internal workloads. The stack must deploy a VPC configured with a variable region defaulting to "us-east-1", a resource name prefix variable defaulting to "tfm-aws", instance tenancy defaulting to "default", enabled DNS hostnames (true), enabled DNS support (true), and a main CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16". Provision two private subnets across the first two available availability zones in the region using CIDR blocks specified by a private_subnets list variable defaulting to ["10.0.2.0/24", "10.0.3.0/24"], paired with two dedicated private route tables and subnet route table associations. Additionally, associate an S3 VPC gateway endpoint with both private route tables, and associate a shared network ACL with the private subnets containing an inbound rule and an outbound rule configured from variable lists public_inbound_acl_rules and public_outbound_acl_rules (the inbound rule defaulting to rule number 100 allowing TCP ports 1024 to 65535 from "0.0.0.0/0" for return traffic, and the outbound rule defaulting to rule number 100 allowing only TCP port 443 to "0.0.0.0/0").

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive Amazon SQS messaging module supporting standard and FIFO queues, custom queue policies, dead-letter queues, redrive policies, and SSE encryption. Primary queue creation must be controlled by a boolean variable create defaulting to true, handling name or name_prefix patterns while automatically managing the .fifo suffix for FIFO queues (fifo_queue defaulting to false). SQS managed server-side encryption (sqs_managed_sse_enabled defaulting to true) must apply automatically whenever a custom KMS master key ID is omitted. Option for attached queue policies must be governed by a create_queue_policy flag defaulting to false, merging source and override policy document strings or rendering custom policy statements where resource defaults to the queue ARN when unspecified. When dead-letter queue creation is toggled on via create_dlq (defaulting to false), the template must provision a corresponding dead-letter queue (inheriting FIFO configuration, default name suffixing "-dlq", and fallback encryption settings from the main queue), attach a redrive policy to the main queue setting maxReceiveCount to 5, and attach a redrive allow policy to the dead-letter queue restricting redrive permissions byQueue to the main queue ARN when create_dlq_redrive_allow_policy is true (defaulting to true).

We need a Terraform template that creates an AWS Config compliance auditing and security monitoring stack to track configuration changes and enforce security rules across all supported resources in the account. The stack must deploy an IAM role using a name generated from a naming convention module (defaulting to "config" with petname fallback when null or empty) paired with the AWS_ConfigRole managed policy, write permissions to a force-destroy-enabled S3 snapshot storage bucket, and an inline policy permitting SNS publish operations. An AWS Config configuration recorder must capture all supported global and regional resource types and deliver snapshot records with an S3 key prefix of "awsconfig/records" to the snapshot bucket while streaming notifications to an SNS topic bearing the resource name that is encrypted with a dedicated customer-managed KMS key with automatic rotation. Additionally, the template must provision a set of eleven managed AWS Config rules evaluated every twenty-four hours or upon configuration changes: "cloudtrail-enabled" (CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED), "iam-pw-policy" (IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY), "ec2-vpc" (INSTANCES_IN_VPC), "root-mfa-enabled" (ROOT_ACCOUNT_MFA_ENABLED), "acm-expiration-check" (ACM_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRATION_CHECK), "ebs-inuse-check" (EC2_VOLUME_INUSE_CHECK), "ec2-imdsv2-check" (EC2_IMDSV2_CHECK), "rds-encrypted" (RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED), "rds-private" (RDS_INSTANCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK), "rds-private-snapshots" (RDS_SNAPSHOTS_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED), and "required-tags" (REQUIRED_TAGS checking for "terraform.io" and "environment" tags specifically scoped to "S3::Bucket" resources).

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM role and policy baseline required to initialize and operate AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) across replication, conversion, failback, and recovery instances. The stack must provision six service roles under the "/service-role/" path: AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryAgentRole and AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryFailbackRole (both allowing drs.amazonaws.com to assume the role and set source identity, conditioned on the calling account ID and source identity prefixes "s-" and "i-", respectively), alongside AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryConversionServerRole, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstanceRole, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryReplicationServerRole, and AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstanceWithLaunchActionsRole (all assuming ec2.amazonaws.com). Attach corresponding AWS-managed policies (AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryAgentPolicy, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryFailbackPolicy, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryConversionServerPolicy, AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstancePolicy, and AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryReplicationServerPolicy) to their respective service roles, while attaching both AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstancePolicy and AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore to AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryRecoveryInstanceWithLaunchActionsRole. Finally, create a root-path initializer role named AWSElasticDisasterRecoveryInitializerRole that allows the current calling identity user ID to assume it, bound to a custom InitializePolicy permitting service initialization, instance profile creation, PassRole actions for EC2 and DRS services, service-linked role creation for AWSServiceRoleForElasticDisasterRecovery, full EC2 actions, and role policy attachments restricted to the DRS managed policies.

We need a Terraform template that creates a dual-VPC isolated production network architecture consisting of an external VPC and an internal VPC in the region to segregate public-facing traffic from internal workloads. The external VPC must be configured with CIDR block "10.41.0.0/16", enable DNS support and DNS hostnames, apply tags for Name ("Production External"), purpose ("Production External VPC"), and environment ("prod"), and manage its default security group with no ingress or egress rules. Four subnets must be provisioned in the external VPC across the first four availability zones in the region using CIDR blocks "10.41.0.0/24" ("Subnet0-1a"), "10.41.1.0/24" ("Subnet1-1b"), "10.41.2.0/24" ("Subnet2-1c"), and "10.41.3.0/24" ("Subnet3-1d"), all attached to an Internet Gateway named "External GW" via a custom route table that is set as the main route table association for the VPC and associated with all four subnets. The external VPC default network ACL must adopt rules for ICMP egress (rule 100 allow), all-traffic egress (rule 150 allow), and all-traffic ingress (rule 100 allow) from "0.0.0.0/0". The internal VPC must be created with CIDR block "10.40.0.0/16", default tenancy, tags for Name ("Production Internal"), purpose ("Production Internal VPC"), and environment ("prod"), managing its default security group with no ingress or egress rules. Four internal subnets must be created in the internal VPC across the first four availability zones in the region using CIDR blocks "10.40.0.0/24" ("Subnet0-1a"), "10.40.1.0/24" ("Subnet1-1b"), "10.40.2.0/24" ("Subnet2-1c"), and "10.40.3.0/24" ("Subnet3-1d"), bound to a default network ACL that explicitly restricts rules to ICMP egress (rule 100 allow), all-traffic egress (rule 150 allow), and ICMP ingress (rule 100 allow) from "0.0.0.0/0".

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained VPC networking baseline and security group configuration for a data stack environment supporting multi-AZ databases, bastion access, CI/CD automation, proxy load balancing, and ETL compute nodes. The VPC must be created with CIDR block "10.255.0.0/16" named "Quasar" and tagged with Application "dosomething-quasar", Environment "production", and Stack "data", housing two subnets for a multi-AZ RDS setup with CIDR blocks "10.255.100.0/24" (tagged Name "Quasar RDS - 1A") and "10.255.101.0/24" (tagged Name "Quasar RDS - 1E"). Five dedicated security groups with outbound egress limited to the VPC CIDR must be provisioned within the VPC using the same tagging schema: a "Quasar-Bastion" security group allowing inbound SSH (port 22) only from the placeholder admin range "203.0.113.0/24"; a "Quasar-HA-Proxy" security group allowing inbound HTTP (port 80) and HTTPS (port 443) from everywhere ("0.0.0.0/0") and SSH (port 22) from the Bastion security group; a "Quasar-Jenkins" security group allowing inbound SSH (port 22) from the Bastion security group and port 8080 from the HA-Proxy security group; a "Quasar-ETL" security group allowing inbound SSH (port 22) from both the Bastion and Jenkins security groups; and a "Quasar-PostgreSQL" security group allowing inbound PostgreSQL traffic (port 5432) both from everywhere ("0.0.0.0/0") and specifically referenced from the ETL security group.

We need a Terraform template that creates an automated AWS CodeDeploy release pipeline for AWS Lambda blue/green deployments managed via local CLI execution scripts. Global creation controls must be governed by a boolean create variable defaulting to true, accepting a function_name, alias_name, current_version, and target_version alongside optional before_allow_traffic_hook_arn and after_allow_traffic_hook_arn lifecycle hooks. When create_app is true and use_existing_app is false (both defaulting to false), create a Lambda compute platform CodeDeploy application named by app_name, and when create_deployment_group is true and use_existing_deployment_group is false (both defaulting to false), provision a deployment group bound to deployment_config_name (defaulting to "CodeDeployDefault.LambdaAllAtOnce") configured with "WITH_TRAFFIC_CONTROL" and "BLUE_GREEN" deployment styles, automatic rollbacks enabled by default on "DEPLOYMENT_STOP_ON_ALARM", optional CloudWatch alarm monitoring, and notification triggers. When create_codedeploy_role is true (defaulting to true), the module must create an IAM role with assume policy for specified CodeDeploy service principals (defaulting to "codedeploy.amazonaws.com"), attach the "AWSCodeDeployRoleForLambda" managed policy, and conditionally attach inline policies granting lambda:InvokeFunction for specified hooks when attach_hooks_policy is true (defaulting to true) or sns:Publish for triggers when attach_triggers_policy is true (defaulting to false). Finally, when create_deployment is true (defaulting to false), construct an AppSpec JSON revision and shell script that uses aws_cli_command (defaulting to "aws") to create and optionally monitor the deployment status with configurable sleep intervals (defaulting get_deployment_sleep_timer to 5 seconds), optionally saving the generated script locally when save_deploy_script is true (defaulting to false) or executing the deployment provisioner via a null resource when run_deployment is true (defaulting to false) with optional uuid-based force_deploy triggers.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, production-grade Amazon S3 private storage bucket with automated compliance policy enforcement, lifecycle management, analytics, and optional inventory reporting. The template must accept a base bucket name defaulting to "benchmark-bucket-tf5x", with optional name prefixes based on the AWS IAM account alias when use_account_alias_prefix is enabled, or use a random suffix prefix when use_random_suffix is set to true. The bucket policy must extend any custom JSON bucket policy passed via custom_bucket_policy to enforce encrypted requests by denying s3:* actions over non-TLS transport ("aws:SecureTransport" equal to "false") and allow S3 service principals to write inventory and analytics data when bucket-owner-full-control ACL is specified. Bucket access blocks must be enabled by default (controlled by enable_s3_public_access_block) to restrict public ACLs and public bucket policies, while object ownership defaults to "BucketOwnerEnforced" under ownership control management. Server-side encryption must default to AES256 unless kms_master_key_id is provided to enable "aws:kms" encryption, with bucket_key_enabled defaulting to false. Versioning status must default to "Enabled", bucket force destroy defaults to false, transition default minimum object size is set to "all_storage_classes_128K", and lifecycle rules must automatically abort incomplete multipart uploads after 14 days while transitioning noncurrent versions to "STANDARD_IA" after 30 days and expiring them after 365 days. Storage class analytics defaulting to enabled (enable_analytics set to true) must write export data under prefix "_AWSBucketAnalytics/" with a 30-day lifecycle expiration, while optional bucket inventory (enable_bucket_inventory defaulting to false) writes ORC-formatted reports under prefix "_AWSBucketInventory/" on a "Weekly" schedule with a 14-day lifecycle expiration. Finally, logging to an external target bucket is conditionally enabled when logging_bucket is specified using a target prefix of "s3/" followed by the bucket's id and a trailing slash, transfer acceleration status is conditionally configured when transfer_acceleration is not null, bucket ACLs are applied when s3_bucket_acl is set, and CORS rules are dynamically applied from a cors_rules list.

We need a Terraform template that creates account-wide security baselines and IAM governance structures for managing administrative and developer access. The stack must enforce an account-wide IAM password policy with a minimum length of 12 requiring uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols, and allowing password changes, while enabling account-level S3 public access block settings (blocking public ACLs, public policies, ignoring public ACLs, and restricting public buckets). Create two IAM groups named using a configurable group_name_prefix variable (defaulting to "app") appended with "_developer" and "_admin". For developer access, attach AWS-managed policies for IAMReadOnlyAccess, IAMUserChangePassword, and IAMUserSSHKeys, alongside custom policies for managing personal access keys, virtual MFA devices (requiring MFA to deactivate), MFA-gated S3 access (denying s3:CreateBucket outside a single designated AWS region and denying all s3:* access to a specific remote-state S3 bucket and its contents), and MFA-gated access for EC2, ELB, CloudWatch, AutoScaling, and specific EC2/AutoScaling service-linked roles. For administrative access, create an IAM role named "admin" that can be assumed by the account root principal, attached to a policy granting full administrative access conditioned on active MFA, and attach a policy to the admin group allowing members to assume this admin role when MFA is present.

We need a Terraform template that creates a data-driven AWS CI/CD pipeline orchestration framework parsing a YAML configuration file specified by the config variable. The stack must dynamically provision S3 artifact and build cache buckets, an optional default CodePipeline IAM role under path "/terraforest/" permitting CodeCommit, CodeBuild, and ECR access, and CodeStar connections for Bitbucket, GitHub, or GitHub Enterprise Server source providers. Pipelines must be configured with dynamic stages supporting CodeCommit, S3, ECR, or CodeStar sources, alongside approval, CodeBuild, and Lambda actions instantiated via external modules. Additionally, configure EventBridge event rules and targets driven by custom IAM roles named by prefixing "terrabits-" to each pipeline's name, allowing codepipeline:StartPipelineExecution to trigger pipelines via CodeCommit branch changes, CodeCommit tag changes, cron schedule expressions, or custom EventBridge event patterns.

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained AWS security group module supporting either a newly created security group or, alternatively, adding rules to an existing security group supplied as an input parameter alongside the target VPC ID, controlled by toggles for overall module creation and whether to create a new group. The new security group should support a configurable create-before-destroy lifecycle and rule-revocation-on-delete behavior, with separate, flexible lists of ingress and egress rule objects for both the new and existing security-group paths, each rule specifying exactly one of an IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR block, a referenced security group ID, or a managed prefix list ID alongside its protocol and port range, and defaulting to allowing all outbound IPv4 traffic. Additionally, the template must optionally create a customer-managed EC2 prefix list with a configurable address family and maximum entry count, populated from a list of CIDR entries, whenever prefix list creation is enabled and no existing prefix list IDs are supplied.

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive set of twenty-seven DynamoDB tables and associated Systems Manager parameters to serve as the database layer for a decentralized wallet and file management backend application. All tables must be configured with on-demand billing mode ("PAY_PER_REQUEST"), tagged with their respective resource Name and Environment (defaulting to "dev"), and protected against accidental deletion using lifecycle prevention rules. The database schema must provision "near-app-actions-mapping" (hash key "appId"), "near-app-actions-master" (hash key "actionId"), "near-app-categories" (hash key "categoryId"), "near-apps" (hash key "appId" with GSI "categoryId-Index" projecting ALL), "near-connected-apps" (hash key "connectionId" with GSIs "userId-Index" and "appId-Index" projecting ALL), "near-contacts" (hash key "contactId" with GSI "userId-contactId-index" projecting ALL), "near-fiat-tokens" (hash key "symbol"), "near-files-invitations" (hash key "pk", range key "sk", stream type "NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES", and TTL on "ttl"), "near-files" (hash key "walletId", range key "fileId", stream type "NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES", TTL on "ttl", with GSIs "ownerId-walletId-index", "hash-index", and "ownerId-fileId-index" projecting ALL), "near-folders" (hash key "walletId", range key "id"), "near-hashes" (hash key "hk", range key "sk", stream type "NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES", with GSI "hk1-sk1-Index" projecting ALL), "near-hidden" (hash key "id"), "near-nft-access-requests" (hash key "requestId" with GSIs "nftId-Index", "ownerId-Index", and "requesterId-Index" projecting ALL), "near-nft-activities" (hash key "activityId", range key "created" as number, with GSI "nftId-Index" projecting ALL), "near-nft-categories" (hash key "categoryId"), "near-nft-collections" (hash key "collectionId" with GSI "OwnerIdIndex" projecting ALL), "near-nft-offers" (hash key "offerId" with GSI "nftId-Index" projecting ALL), "near-nft-shares" (hash key "shareId" with GSIs "nftId-Index", "ownerWalletId-Index", and "recipientWalletId-Index" projecting ALL), "near-nfts" (hash key "nftId" with GSIs "ownerWalletId-Index" and "transactionId-Index" projecting ALL), "near-otp" (hash key "userId", range key "ttl" as number with TTL on "ttl"), "near-shared-files" (hash key "fileId", range key "userId"), "near-storage" (hash key "pk", range key "sk", stream type "NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES", TTL on "ttl", with GSI "GSI1" using "pk1" and "sk1" projecting ALL), "near-transactions" (hash key "transactionId" with GSIs "senderWalletId-Index", "receiverWalletId-Index", "jobId-created-Index", and "parentId-created-Index" projecting ALL), "near-users" (hash key "userId" with GSIs "PhoneIndex" and "EmailIndex" projecting ALL), "near-wallets-blockchain" (hash key "wallet_id"), "near-wallets-private" (hash key "walletId" with GSI "UserIdIndex" using range key "walletId" projecting ALL), and "near-wallets" (hash key "walletId", stream type "NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES", with GSIs "userId-Index", "walletName-Index", and "jobId-Index" projecting ALL). Additionally, store the ARN, table name, and stream ARN as String SSM parameters under "/file-service/dynamodb/invitations/" for "near-files-invitations", "/file-service/dynamodb/files/" for "near-files", "/hashes-service/dynamodb/hashes/" for "near-hashes", "/file-service/dynamodb/storage/" for "near-storage", and under "/wallet-service/dynamodb/wallets/" for "near-wallets".

We need a Terraform template that creates a VPC for application deployments, including public and private subnets, an internet gateway, a NAT gateway, route tables, and network ACLs. The VPC should use a CIDR block of 10.0.0.0/18. The number of availability zones should be configurable, defaulting to all available AZs in the region. The template should allow toggling the creation of public subnets, private subnets, and the NAT gateway via boolean variables. The VPC name should be configurable with a default of "benchmark-vpc". The AWS region should default to us-east-1. All necessary dependencies should be created as part of the stack.

We need a Terraform template that creates a highly customizable VPC module supporting multi-tier subnet architecture and configurable NAT gateway routing. The template must feature a main creation toggle defaulting to true, a configurable VPC CIDR block defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", and options to enable DNS hostnames and DNS support (both defaulting to true). Subnet tiers must support lists of CIDR blocks for public, private, and isolated intra subnets mapped across a provided list of availability zone names or IDs, automatically generating subnet Name tags using configurable tier suffixes ("public", "private", "intra") and availability zone identifiers unless explicit name lists are supplied. When public subnets are present, the module should support map public IP on launch toggles (defaulting to false) and conditionally provision an Internet Gateway based on a creation toggle (defaulting to true) attached to a dedicated public route table with a default 0.0.0.0/0 route. Additionally, when private subnets, public subnets, and NAT gateways are enabled via the NAT gateway toggle (defaulting to false), the module must create Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways up to the minimum count of public or private subnets, establishing individual private route tables with 0.0.0.0/0 NAT routes associated with each private subnet, while intra subnets maintain isolated route tables without external internet routes.

We need a Terraform template that creates a unified, dual-mode API Gateway module capable of provisioning either an HTTP API (v2) or a REST API (v1) with optional VPC links, custom domain mappings, API keys, and custom Lambda authorizers. The API type must be determined by a variable defaulting to "http", using a default API name of "benchmark-api", and deploying stages named using the environment name value followed by the suffix "-stage". For HTTP APIs, the template should support dynamic route mappings, auto-deployed stages, custom domain configurations with TLS 1.2 regional ACM certificates, optional Route 53 alias A records, and HTTP VPC links created across private subnets. For REST APIs, the module must support dynamic resource path mapping, route methods with path parameter overrides, optional IP source restriction resource policies, automatic redeployment triggers, usage plans with API keys saved as SecureString parameters in SSM Parameter Store, and custom Lambda authorizers featuring Node.js 16.x functions, invocation roles, and execution policies. Additionally, when a VPC link is enabled for REST APIs, the setup must automatically provision an internal Network Load Balancer across private subnets, a target group targeting an ALB ID at a configurable TCP port (defaulting to 443) with HTTPS health checks, a target group attachment, a TCP listener, and an API Gateway VPC link targeting the load balancer ARN.

We need a Terraform template that creates the IAM roles, policies, attachments, and instance profiles required to support an Amazon EKS control plane and worker node group with Cluster Autoscaler integration. The template must declare a cluster_name variable defaulting to "legion" and establish two IAM roles: one named with a "tf-" prefix followed by the cluster name value for the master control plane, and another named with the same prefix followed by the cluster name value and a "-node" suffix for the worker nodes. The master role must allow assume role trust for the EKS service and attach the AWS managed policies "AmazonEKSClusterPolicy" and "AmazonEKSServicePolicy". The worker node role must allow assume role trust for EC2, attach the managed policies "AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy", "AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy", and "AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly", and be associated with a matching EC2 instance profile whose name follows the same "tf-" prefix, cluster name value, and "-node" suffix pattern. Additionally, the worker node role must be attached to a custom, dynamically-generated IAM policy whose name is prefixed with "eks-worker-autoscaling-" followed by the cluster name value, permitting global describe actions for Auto Scaling groups, Auto Scaling instances, launch configurations, tags, and launch template versions, while restricting capacity modification actions ("autoscaling:SetDesiredCapacity", "autoscaling:TerminateInstanceInAutoScalingGroup", and "autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup") strictly to resources tagged with a key of "kubernetes.io/cluster/" followed by the cluster name value, equal to "owned", and "k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled" equal to "true".

We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained IAM access management infrastructure to support administrative, CI/CD, and serverless deployment workloads. The stack must establish four IAM groups with distinct paths and inline policies: an "admin" group with path "/admin/" granting full wildcard administrative permissions, an "admin-terraform-cloud" group with path "/admin_terraform_cloud/" also granted full wildcard administrative permissions, a "github" group with path "/github/" assigned an inline policy permitting targeted ACM, CloudFront, IAM, Lambda, Route53, S3, and SQS actions, and a "serverless" group with path "/serverless/" assigned a dedicated policy covering ACM, CloudFront, IAM, Lambda, CloudWatch Logs, Route53, S3, and SQS actions. Additionally, the template must provision corresponding IAM users and memberships, specifically "admin" in the admin group, "admin-macbook-pro" in the admin group with an access key, "admin-terraform-cloud" in the admin-terraform-cloud group with an access key, "github" in the github group, and "serverless" in the serverless group. To complete the serverless tooling access, create an IAM role named "serverless" with path "/serverless/" that allows trust assumptions for Lambda and Edge Lambda services, attaching a customer managed policy named "serverless" with path "/serverless/" containing the identical serverless policy permissions.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure IAM access management framework to enforce multi-factor authentication for user self-management and administrative role assumption. The setup must utilize standardized CloudPosse label modules for consistent naming using namespace, environment, name, tags, and attributes variables across both an admin group and a non-admin group. A self-management policy must be attached to both groups allowing members to manage their own passwords, access keys, virtual MFA devices, and list account MFA devices and password policies, while requiring active MFA specifically to deactivate their virtual MFA devices. The admin group must additionally receive a policy granting permission to assume a dedicated admin role, strictly requiring MFA present for both role assumption and the role's trust policy targeting the account root principal. The admin role must be attached to the AWS-managed AdministratorAccess policy, and both groups must conditionally manage user memberships based on provided lists of admin and non-admin user names.

We need a Terraform template that creates a versatile AWS security group management module to manage network access controls for application workloads. The setup must feature a main enable toggle (defaulting to true) and allow toggling between creating a new security group or attaching rules to an existing security group. If a new security group is requested and no VPC ID is supplied, the template must automatically provision a fallback VPC with CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 to host the security group. Resource naming and tagging must integrate with the git-based label module git::https://github.com/sohanyadav/terraform-aws-labels.git?ref=v1.0.0, appending -sg for new security groups and -prefix-list for managed prefix lists. The template must support optional managed prefix list creation when enabled without pre-existing prefix list IDs, defaulting to IPv4 address family and a maximum of 5 entries. Both new and existing security group rule management must support separate categorized rule inputs for ingress and egress based on CIDR blocks, self-referencing rules, source security group IDs, and prefix lists (defaulting to the newly created prefix list when unspecified).

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom Amazon EKS cluster named "demo-eks" with unmanaged worker nodes deployed via a CloudFormation-managed Auto Scaling Group in a new VPC across three availability zones in us-east-1, ensuring the AWS provider applies a default tag of "kubernetes.io/cluster/demo-eks" set to "owned". First, create a 10.0.0.0/16 VPC with DNS support and hostnames, an internet gateway, a public subnet hosting a NAT gateway, and three private subnets (one per availability zone) routed through that NAT gateway, then provision the EKS control plane with a private-only API endpoint and secrets encrypted by a customer-managed KMS key, attached to those private subnets, utilizing an IAM role named "eksClusterRole" that includes the standard EKS cluster and VPC resource controller policies plus permission to use that KMS key. For the worker nodes, generate a 4096-bit RSA TLS private key, save it locally to "~/.ssh/eks-aws.pem", and register it as an AWS key pair named "eks_kp". Create a dedicated node security group allowing outbound traffic only within the VPC CIDR, unrestricted internal communication between nodes, and tightly scoped TCP ingress and egress rules on ports 443 and 1025-65535 to permit two-way communication with the EKS control plane's security group. Provision an IAM role named "eks-demo-node" with managed policies for EKS worker nodes, CNI, ECR read-only, and SSM core management, and attach it to an instance profile. Next, configure an EC2 launch template using a t3.medium instance, a 30 GB gp2 root volume, required IMDSv2 HTTP tokens with a hop limit of 2, the latest Amazon Linux 2 EKS-optimized AMI retrieved via SSM, and a base64-encoded user-data bootstrap script that connects to the cluster and signals a CloudFormation stack upon completion. After incorporating a 30-second delay to allow the launch template to settle, deploy a CloudFormation stack named "eks-cluster-stack" to provision the Auto Scaling Group across the private subnets with a minimum size of 1, desired capacity of 3, and maximum size of 4, ensuring it incorporates an update policy for rolling updates with a maximum batch size of 1, a minimum of 3 instances in service, and a 5-minute pause time. Finally, output the node instance role ARN, the node security group ID, and the newly created Auto Scaling Group ID returned directly by the CloudFormation stack.

We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, highly durable remote state management architecture for multiple EKS stacks, utilizing an S3 backend in us-east-1 with cross-region replication to a second AWS region. The deployment must provision a primary S3 bucket named dynamically with the AWS account ID, enforcing versioning, strict public access blocks, and a bucket policy that explicitly denies non-SSL requests. All objects in the primary bucket must be encrypted server-side by default using a new custom KMS key configured with a 7-day deletion window and automatic key rotation. For disaster recovery, provision a replica S3 bucket in that second region with identical versioning, SSL enforcement, and public access blocks, secured by its own dedicated replica KMS key. Configure S3 cross-region replication on the primary bucket to automatically replicate KMS-encrypted objects to the replica bucket, attaching an IAM role with the precise permissions required to read the source objects, decrypt them using the primary KMS key, and encrypt them at the destination using the replica key. To support concurrent operations, iterate through a provided map of stack names and regions to deploy individual pay-per-request DynamoDB tables keyed by "LockID" for each stack's state locking, alongside dedicated IAM policies that grant stack-specific access to their respective DynamoDB table, S3 bucket prefix, and KMS key operations. Finally, the template must automatically generate a local "backend.tf" file for each stack within a relative "eks-stacks" directory to seamlessly integrate these backend configurations into our workflows, ensuring all created resources are tagged with a standardized set of state management labels.

We need a Terraform template that creates two IAM roles assumable by Lambda for automating DynamoDB backups: a role named "create_ddb_backup_role" with a policy named "create_ddb_backup_policy" allowing it to create DynamoDB backups, and a role named "remove_ddb_backup_role" with a policy named "remove_ddb_backup_policy" allowing it to list and delete DynamoDB backups. Both roles should also share a customer-managed policy named "lambda_logging" that grants CloudWatch Logs write permissions, and the template should output both roles.

We need a Terraform template that creates a cross-account IAM role named "CloudHealth-IAM-Role" that the CloudHealth SaaS platform's AWS account can assume using an external ID condition, together with a customer-managed IAM policy of the same name granting broad read-only describe, list and get permissions across AWS services for cost and usage analysis, attached to the role.

We need a Terraform template that creates a cross-region S3 replication setup for log buckets tagged with Env "dev", spanning four regions: two source regions (the first being us-east-1) and two separate replica regions. In the primary source region, create two source buckets named "log1a.veerum" and "log1b.veerum", and in the second source region two source buckets named "log2a.veerum" and "log2b.veerum", each followed by a hyphen and the current AWS account ID. In each replica region, create four replica buckets, one per source bucket, named after the source bucket with a "-replica1" or "-replica2" suffix respectively followed by the account ID. Every bucket must be private with versioning enabled, block all public access, and use default SSE-KMS encryption with a customer-managed KMS key created in its own region, aliased "alias/sourcekey1", "alias/sourcekey2", "alias/replicakey1", and "alias/replicakey2". Each source bucket needs two enabled replication rules covering all objects, including SSE-KMS encrypted objects, that copy them in the STANDARD storage class to its matching replica bucket in each replica region, re-encrypting with that region's replica key. Replication should run under an IAM role that S3 can assume, with a customer-managed policy allowing it to read the source buckets and object versions, replicate objects and deletes into the replica buckets, decrypt with the source keys, and encrypt with the replica keys.
